..
Distant Tropical Storm Dujuan has moved north of 25N and has exited
the region. Dujuan continues to steer relatively drier air south of 
20N, leading to spotty showers across Tinian and Saipan, then showers
become increasingly scattered across Guam and Rota, closer in 
proximity to the trailing band of monsoonal moisture and convergence.
Scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms prevail across the 
region, moreso across Guam and Rota through Saturday, then showers 
spread northward across Tinian and Saipan early next week. A brief 
period of numerous showers are expected to build across southern Guam
waters overnight, with locally heavy showers and occasional gusts to
25 mph possible across Guam. The main band of monsoonal moisture 
continues to linger near and south of Guam, with model guidance 
showing some potential of a nearby weak disturbance forming in the 
monsoon trough early next week. Depending on this scenario or if 
there is a northward shift in the monsoon trough, this could 
potentially result in periods of scattered to numerous showers with 
moderate to strong gusts early next week. 

Marine...
Gentle to moderate west to southwest winds decrease to light to 
gentle over the weekend, then shift to the south to southeast 
next week. Combined seas of 5 to 7 feet are comprised of southwest
monsoon swell, northerly swell from distant Tropical Storm 
Dujuan, and light northeast swell. Seas are expected to subside to
4 to 6 feet over the weekend and early next week due to a slight
decrease in wind waves and swells.

Eastern Micronesia...
A rather slow-moving stagnant pattern remains in place, with a ridge
axis centered over Pohnpei, a slightly elevated low just north-
northwest of Majuro. An increased pressure gradient between the two 
from near Pohnpei southeast to Kosrae. Here, gentle to moderate winds
persist, and this looks to continue through Sunday night. Then, the
ridge axis weakens some as it drifts west, allowing the gradient to
slacken.

However, this amplified (for the tropics) pattern is allowing for a
wedge of moisture to stretch from near Pohnpei to Kosrae, rounding
the base of a trough west of Makin, then shooting north as it grazes
Majuro to the east. Given the slow progression of the synoptic
pattern observed over the last few days, and with model trends
showing more of the same, we opted to go with a long period of 
scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms at Pohnpei and Kosrae, 
while eventually dropping them back to isolated showers at Majuro 
early next week. Although, this may need to be increased in later 
forecasts if the Monsoon Trough sinks south far enough to have an 
influence, as the pattern reorientates itself over the next several 
days.

As for marine conditions, as mentioned above, gentle to moderate
winds will persist through Sunday night for Pohnpei and Kosrae,
becoming light to gentle thereafter. Light to gentle winds will
prevail at Majuro throughout the forecast period. Seas will hold in
the 4 to 6 foot range.

Western Micronesia...
Satellite imagery shows scattered showers over Yap and isolated
showers over Palau and Chuuk. Altimetry shows combined seas are
between 5 and 8 feet across the region. 

Quiet conditions are currently in place across western Micronesia.
Widely scattered showers are seen across Yap, while isolated showers
are seen elsewhere. The monsoon tail that features heavier showers
has mostly cut-off from Tropical Storm Dujuan. This monsoon tail may
continue to shift north over the next day before shifting south by
Sunday or Monday. This will place the focus of heavier showers over
Yap late this weekend and into next week. The eastern edge of the
monsoon pattern will interact with a surface ridge near Chuuk. This
will allow for an increase in showers across Chuuk State Saturday
night and persisting into next week. Quiet conditions are expected
early in the forecast cycle for Palau, then late this weekend,
converging inflow winds into a tropical disturbance west of the
Marianas will help bring showers and thunderstorms.

The Small Craft Advisory for Yap was expired at 5 PM ChST today.
Choppy seas will remain possible through Sunday due to an elevated
west swell. Elsewhere seas look to remain benign through the period,
but some choppy seas will be possible near heavier showers.
